clue.text: Balance cost in Europe being reorganised

indicators.note: letters being reorganised are put into a fresh order, so the three words before are shuffled

explanation.surface: An economist's remark that rearranging prices across Europe evens things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being reorganised' shuffles the twelve letters of COST IN EUROPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterweight is a balance: something that offsets an opposing force or weight.

clue.text: Bank clerk in middle of stick-up, looking greyer

indicators.note: the middle of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

parts.note: ashier means paler, more like the grey of ash

explanation.surface: A bank worker caught in a hold-up turns pale with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes C, the centre of STICKUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who handles money at a bank counter is a teller, also called a cashier.

clue.text: Country leaving EU shower — start of European state?

parts.note: the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union
a shower is a spell of rain

indicators.note: start of takes just the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Post-Brexit politics: a nation leaves the bloc while another sits at Europe's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eastern European nation is a sovereign state; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Leniency later on dispensed by Church

indicators.note: by puts the church abbreviation beside the shuffled letters
dispensed suggests the letters are handed out afresh in a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Mercy later handed out by the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensed' shuffles LATER ON into TOLERAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is forbearance, a lenient willingness to put up with things.

clue.text: Come-uppance for Queen virtuoso's imitation

indicators.note: in a down clue come-uppance means coming up, so the royal letters are read upwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a pro is an expert, a virtuoso

explanation.surface: A star performer gets their just deserts for mimicking the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come-uppance' splits as 'come up', a reversal signal in a down light; the punishment sense is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy or imitation of an original.

clue.text: Rich, old and posh covered with endless wealth

indicators.note: covered with means the posh letter sits inside the shortened word
endless means the abundance word loses its final letter

parts.note: plenty means abundance, wealth
U means upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A description of an aristocrat: elderly, upper-class and smothered in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts PLENTY to PLENT, which wraps U.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means luxuriously wealthy, displaying great riches.

clue.text: Foreign lady dressed up in sarong, I suppose

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the concealed letters are read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad is presumably wearing a sarong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to ARONGIS inside 'sarong, I suppose'; 'dressed up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, so a lady from abroad.

clue.text: Detailed interest over lesson's unmatched

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
detailed means losing its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: interest on savings is income
a parable is a story carrying a moral lesson

explanation.surface: A boast that close attention to a lesson has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' is de-tailed: INCOME minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incomparable is beyond comparison, having no equal.

clue.text: Inspirational passage?

parts.note: inspiration is literally breathing in, so the passage it travels through is a nasal opening

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspirational' looks like praise for an uplifting text, but here it means breathing in; the 'passage' is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is inhaled through each opening of the nose, a literal passage for inspiration.

clue.text: Carried on quietly, perhaps?

indicators.note: on says the carried word sits after the other piece

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
lugged means carried with effort

explanation.surface: Someone kept going without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: LUGGED goes 'on' P. Read whole, to plug away is to carry on steadily, often quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plugging away at something means persisting doggedly, i.e. continuing with a task.

clue.text: Special permission over wearing fashionable pants inside

indicators.note: wearing means the letter is clothed by the shuffled letters
fashionable read as fashioned means the letters are shaped into something new

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A dress-code exemption for wearing trendy underwear indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' reads as 'fashioned', an anagram signal, and 'wearing' puts the cricket over (O) inside the rearranged letters (DISPENSATIN); 'pants' is fodder, not a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensation is an exemption from a rule granted by authority.

clue.text: Actor Hardy taking lead in 'Inception'

indicators.note: taking means the first name of the comedian takes in another letter

parts.note: Oliver Hardy was the large half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A film-casting note: comedy star Hardy landing a part in the movie Inception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' is not Tom Hardy of Inception but Oliver Hardy; 'lead in' gives the I of 'Inception'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and screen performer.

clue.text: Demanding euro's scrapped after negative vote's returned

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the turned-round vote
returned means the word for the vote is turned round

parts.note: a no is a vote against

indicators.note: scrapped suggests the currency letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken with its S as letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A political grumble: the euro was dropped after a referendum went the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the negative vote round and 'scrapped' shuffles the currency word (EROUS), which comes 'after'; the 's of euro's supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome, one that makes heavy demands on you.

clue.text: Power push producing witch hunt

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to urge is to push or press someone

explanation.surface: Pressure from those in authority leads to the persecution of dissidents.
explanation.definitionFit: A political clean-out of opponents is a campaign of persecution, just like a witch hunt.

clue.text: Almost tense and hurt bearing ordeal

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
to mar is to damage or spoil
E (east) is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Nearly strained and wounded while enduring a terrible trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like 'enduring' but is a compass direction, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrowing experience is often called a living bad dream, i.e. an ordeal.

clue.text: Finally digging a hole within enclosure?

definitions.text: Finally digging a hole within enclosure?

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the next word
within places the hole inside the enclosure

parts.note: a ring is a circular enclosure
a den is a hole or lair

explanation.surface: At last breaking ground in a fenced plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, digging a hole within a fenced plot describes the pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging holes in an enclosed plot is typical of tending a garden.

clue.text: Grass accepting villain's regret backing storyteller

indicators.note: accepting means the informer takes the villain inside

parts.note: to grass is to inform, and an informer is a rat
a con is a convict, a villain

indicators.note: backing means the word for regret is read in reverse

parts.note: rue means regret

explanation.surface: An informer, taking on a crook's remorse, supports a teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer (RAT), not the lawn. 'backing' turns RUE into EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone skilled at telling anecdotes, a storyteller.

clue.text: Spiked attachment's trick to take on slope

indicators.note: to take on means the swindle word takes the slope inside it

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a ramp is a slope

explanation.surface: A climber's spiked gear is a ruse for tackling an incline.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked metal plate fixed to a boot for gripping ice.

clue.text: Fertiliser can's tipped controlled amount

indicators.note: tipped means the container word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
a rate is a measured quantity or amount, as in a dosing rate

explanation.surface: A gardener tips out a measured dose of plant feed from a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' turns TIN into NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrate compounds are widely used in agricultural fertilisers.

clue.text: Small prongs urging rider's steed initially

definitions.text: Small prongs urging rider's steed initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the preceding five words

explanation.surface: A description of riding gear: little points that drive a horse on.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiked heel attachments goad a horse forward, small prongs used by riders.

clue.text: Reinforce part of post if fencing

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice on strengthening a fence by adding posts.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen something is to strengthen or make it more rigid.

clue.text: A French redhead in stockings upset by stallion

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in places the head letter inside the stockings

parts.note: hose are stockings
the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A French redhead in stockings, rattled by a stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is the head of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhorse a rider is to throw them from the saddle, as a bucking stallion might.

clue.text: Shot — remain in sack

indicators.note: in puts the word for remain inside the one for sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
to last is to remain or endure

explanation.surface: Someone, gunned down, stays tucked up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' is the informal word for bed, as in 'hit the sack'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasted can mean fired at or struck with gunfire, i.e. shot.

clue.text: Stay fit to support daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it follows

parts.note: well means healthy, fit

explanation.surface: Keeping in shape to look after one's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or remain somewhere, to stay.

clue.text: English meat and French 'appellation'

parts.note: pith is the essential core or meat of something
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A menu item: English meat accompanied by a French name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' is the substance or core of an argument (PITH), not food.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or title given to someone, an appellation.

clue.text: Pay for former wife, French dish squeezing one

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: squeezing means the dish holds the numeral within it

parts.note: pâté is a French meat paste
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone must cover the bill for their ex and a French dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a wrong is to make amends or atone, paying for it.

clue.text: Cool iron leading to oddly random blaze

indicators.note: leading to puts the earlier pieces in front of the picked letters

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Ironing at a cool setting somehow leads to a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' and 'iron' suggest laundry, but they are IN and FE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a huge raging fire, a blaze.

clue.text: Changing line electing wit

indicators.note: changing letters means altering their order, so the two words after are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A voter switching sides because they picked the cleverer candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' shuffles the letters of LINE ELECTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit can mean mental sharpness or brains, as in 'use your wits'.
